items.title: Quick Start Guide
items.content: Welcome to Scladapp. This guide walks you through everything from creating your school account to enrolling your first student. For every screen it lists each field you will fill in, tells you which ones are required (marked *), and shows what to do next. Follow the steps in order so classes, subjects, teachers and students connect correctly.

blocks.text: Welcome to Scladapp. This guide walks you through everything from creating your school account to enrolling your first student. For every screen it lists each field you will fill in, tells you which ones are required (marked *), and shows what to do next. Follow the steps in order so classes, subjects, teachers and students connect correctly.

steps.desc: Click Get Started on the homepage. The setup wizard has four screens (School details, Location, Admin account, Plan and payment) plus an email verification code. A progress indicator at the top shows where you are, and you can go Back to change anything before you finish.

blocks.text: Click Get Started on the homepage. The setup wizard has four screens (School details, Location, Admin account, Plan and payment) plus an email verification code. A progress indicator at the top shows where you are, and you can go Back to change anything before you finish.
Nothing is created until the last screen, so you can safely go back and edit earlier answers.

steps.desc: Fill in the basic identity of your school. All five fields are required; you cannot continue until each one is filled.

blocks.text: Fill in the basic identity of your school. All five fields are required; you cannot continue until each one is filled.
School Logo * - upload an image of your school crest or logo. It represents your school across the app.
School Name * - the full official name of the school.
School Slogan * - your school motto or tagline.
School Phone * - the main contact number of the school.
School Email * - the official school email address. It must be a valid email format (for example info@yourschool.com).

steps.desc: Tell us where the school is located. All three fields are required.

blocks.text: Tell us where the school is located. All three fields are required.
Country * - choose Nigeria, Ghana or Kenya.
State * - the state or region where the school is.
Address * - the full street address of the school.

steps.desc: Create the main administrator account. This is the login you will use to manage the whole school.

blocks.text: Create the main administrator account. This is the login you will use to manage the whole school.
Admin Username * - the name you will sign in with.
Admin Email * - the email you will sign in with. It must be valid, and it is the address that receives the verification code. Use an email you can open right now.

Password * - must pass all four checks: at least 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, at least one number, and at least one special character (for example ! @ # $ %). A strength meter shows your progress, and you cannot continue while the password is too weak.
Confirm Password * - type the same password again. The two must match exactly.

steps.desc: After the admin account screen, a 6-digit one-time code is sent to the Admin Email you entered. Type the 6 digits to prove the address is yours. Once accepted, a green Verified badge appears next to the email.

blocks.text: After the admin account screen, a 6-digit one-time code is sent to the Admin Email you entered. Type the 6 digits to prove the address is yours. Once accepted, a green Verified badge appears next to the email.
If the code does not arrive, check your spam or junk folder and request a new code.
If you typed the email wrongly, go Back, correct it and request a new code.

steps.step: Screen 4: Choose a plan and pay
steps.desc: Review your details and choose how you want to subscribe. The review panel summarises your Admin Account (username and email) and School Info (name, phone, email, location) so you can confirm everything is correct.

blocks.text: Review your details and choose how you want to subscribe. The review panel summarises your Admin Account (username and email) and School Info (name, phone, email, location) so you can confirm everything is correct.

Plan * - pick one of the available plans. Each plan card shows its name, description, price and what is included (for example sub-admin limits and unlimited students and staff on paid plans). The free trial plan shows Free and needs no payment.
Billing Cycle - for paid plans choose Monthly, Quarterly or Yearly. Quarterly and yearly are discounted compared with paying monthly.
Number of months, quarters or years - how many billing periods you want to pay for in one go. The label changes with the cycle you chose.
Included Features - a read-only list of what the selected plan gives you.
Payment Summary - shows the plan, cycle, number of periods, any discount and the total you will pay.
Terms and Conditions * - tick I agree to the Terms and Conditions. The final button stays disabled until this box is ticked.

steps.desc: On a free plan click the create button. On a paid plan click the pay button and complete payment in the secure Paystack window. If you close the window without paying, no school is created and you can try again.

blocks.text: On a free plan click the create button. On a paid plan click the pay button and complete payment in the secure Paystack window. If you close the window without paying, no school is created and you can try again.
When setup succeeds you are logged in automatically and taken to your school admin dashboard. You can also sign in later with the Admin Username or Admin Email and the password you created.
New schools get a free trial period. After it ends, a paid subscription is needed to keep creating and editing data.

steps.desc: Open Staff in the sidebar and click Create New Staff Member. Add everyone who works at the school (principal, bursar, teachers, secretaries and so on). Only a few fields are required; the rest can be filled in later by editing the profile.

blocks.text: Open Staff in the sidebar and click Create New Staff Member. Add everyone who works at the school (principal, bursar, teachers, secretaries and so on). Only a few fields are required; the rest can be filled in later by editing the profile.
Personal Information: Staff Photo, Full Name *, Email Address *, Phone Number *, WhatsApp number, Date of Birth and Gender (Male, Female or Other).
Identity / bio: Religion, Marital Status (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed), Nationality, State of Origin, LGA of origin, Place of birth, Tribe / ethnic group, NIN, Blood Group and Genotype.
Residence: House number / street, Area / estate, City, LGA of residence, State of residence and Landmark.

Employment Information: Position * (for example Principal, Bursar), Department * (for example Administration, Finance), Qualification (for example M.Ed, B.Sc), Years of Experience, Employment Type (Full-time, Part-time, Contract or Temporary) and Joining Date.
Emergency Contact: Name, Relationship, Phone and WhatsApp number.
Security and Access: you do not type a password. After you click Create Staff Member, a secure link is emailed to the staff member so they can set their own password. The link expires after 48 hours.

steps.desc: A staff member must be registered as a teacher before they can be assigned to a class or subject. Open Teachers and click create.

blocks.text: A staff member must be registered as a teacher before they can be assigned to a class or subject. Open Teachers and click create.
Teacher Code * - a unique ID for the teacher, for example TCH001.

After you pick a staff member, a card previews their staff ID, email, position and department so you can confirm you chose the right person.

steps.desc: Open Classes and click add class. Create one class for every group of students (for example JSS 1 A).

blocks.text: Open Classes and click add class. Create one class for every group of students (for example JSS 1 A).
Class Name * - for example Grade 10 Science.
Class Code * - a short unique code, for example G10-SCI-A.
Class Section * - Section A, B, C, D or E.

steps.desc: Open Subjects and click add subject. Each subject is linked to the classes that take it and the teacher who teaches it in each class.

blocks.text: Open Subjects and click add subject. Each subject is linked to the classes that take it and the teacher who teaches it in each class.
Subject Name * - for example Mathematics.
Subject Code * - for example MATH101.

Stream * - Science Stream, Arts Stream, Commercial Stream, or General (All Streams).

steps.desc: Open Sessions and click Create New Academic Session. The wizard has four steps, and Next stays disabled until the current step is valid.

blocks.text: Open Sessions and click Create New Academic Session. The wizard has four steps, and Next stays disabled until the current step is valid.
Step 1, Session Basics: Session Name * (for example 2025/2026), Session Code *, Session Start Date * and Session End Date *. The dates are checked, so the end date must come after the start date.

Step 2, Student Promotion and Graduation: choose a Promotion Template that defines how students move up. Use the plus button to add a new template and the refresh button to reload the list. After you pick one, the Promotion Analysis shows how many students will be promoted, demoted or graduated; click a card to review the students and change any student's status to Promote, Demote or Graduate. You can skip this step for a brand new school with no previous session.

Step 3, Create Subsessions (terms): for each term fill in Subsession Name * (for example First Term), Term Code * (for example TERM1), Start Date *, End Date * and Grading Template *. The grading template is required and cannot be changed later, so choose carefully.
Step 4, Review: check the session name, duration, promotion template and every term, then create the session.

steps.desc: Open Templates, then Class Promotion Templates, and click Create. This template tells Scladapp which class each student moves to at the end of a session. It is picked later in the Create Session wizard.

blocks.text: Open Templates, then Class Promotion Templates, and click Create. This template tells Scladapp which class each student moves to at the end of a session. It is picked later in the Create Session wizard.
Template Name * - for example Standard Promotion Criteria.
Grade Level - choose Elementary, Secondary or All Levels.
Description - a short note about when to use this template.

Class Promotion Mapping - click Add Promotion Rule for each class. For every rule pick the From Class (the current class) and the To Class (the class students move into). At least one rule is required. Use ALUMNI as the To Class for your graduating class. Use the plus button to create a missing class and the refresh button to reload the class list.
Cover every class, otherwise students in an unmapped class will not be promoted automatically. You can review and change individual students when you create the next session.

steps.step: Step 6: Set up the grading template
steps.desc: Open Templates, then Grading Templates, and click Create. This defines how scores are weighted and converted to letter grades. A grading template is required for every term when you create a session, and it cannot be changed later, so get it right first.

blocks.text: Open Templates, then Grading Templates, and click Create. This defines how scores are weighted and converted to letter grades. A grading template is required for every term when you create a session, and it cannot be changed later, so get it right first.
Template Name * - for example Standard Grading Scale.
Description - a short explanation of the template.

Assessment Fields - click Add Field for each assessment. For every field enter Field Name (for example First Test, Second Test, Exam), Weight (%) and Max Score (for example /30). The weights of all fields must add up to exactly 100%; the Total Weight indicator turns red until they do, and you cannot save until it is 100%.

Grading Scheme - click Add Grade for each grade row. For every row enter Grade Letter (for example A), Min Range (for example 70), Max Range (for example 100), Grade Point (for example 5.0) and Pass/Fail (Yes or No). The ranges must cover 0% to 100% with no gaps in coverage and no overlapping rows; overlapping rows are highlighted.
After saving you can duplicate the template, edit it, or delete one you no longer need.

steps.step: Step 7: Set up the timetable template
steps.desc: Open Templates, then Timetable Templates, and click Create. This defines your school week: school days, number of periods, start and end times and breaks. Class timetables are built from it.

blocks.text: Open Templates, then Timetable Templates, and click Create. This defines your school week: school days, number of periods, start and end times and breaks. Class timetables are built from it.
Template Name * - for example Standard Weekly Timetable.
Schedule Type - Weekly Schedule, Block Schedule, Elementary Schedule, Exam Schedule or Custom Schedule.
Description - an optional note.
Days per Week - tick every school day (Monday to Sunday). At least one day is required.
Periods per Day - enter the number of periods for each ticked day (0 to 12). Each ticked day needs at least 1.
Max Period Duration (minutes) - the longest a single period can run (15 to 120, for example 40).
Daily Schedule Times - set a Start Time and End Time for each ticked day. The end must be after the start, and the day must be long enough to fit all periods (at least 15 minutes each) plus breaks.

Break Configuration - click Add Break for each break. Enter Break Name (for example Morning Break), Duration in minutes (5 to 120), After Period (the period it follows) and tick Apply to Days. A break must apply to at least one day and must come after a period that exists on that day.
Click Preview to see the weekly grid. Any errors are listed so you can fix them, then save the template and activate it.

Currency - Nigerian Naira (NGN), US Dollar (USD), British Pound (GBP) or Euro (EUR).
Due Date Description - when the bill is due, for example 30 days after term start.
Allow Installments - tick it if parents can pay in parts. Then set Number of Installments (2 to 12) and Minimum Payment (the smallest amount accepted per payment).

Available Placeholders - tick the default placeholders you want, such as school_name, date, time, recipient_name, student_name, parent_name, session, subsession, subject, class, section, teacher_name, grade and academic_year. Announcement Content Template * - the message body, written in the rich text editor (bold, italic, lists, links and so on). Click a placeholder button to insert it at the cursor.
Delivery channel - new templates are sent by Email by default.
Click Preview to see how it looks. When you save a new template, the email layout editor opens so you can style the header, footer, colours and images of the email.

items.title: Subscription & Plans
items.content: Every school runs on a subscription plan. Plans control how many sub-admins you can add, how much file storage you get, and paid extras such as a hosted school website. Students and staff are unlimited on every plan. This guide shows where to manage your plan, what each screen contains, how to pay, and what happens when a subscription ends.

steps.step: Compare plans before you sign up
steps.desc: Open the Pricing page from the website menu to compare plans without logging in. Each plan card shows its price, what is included, and a button to get started.

blocks.text: Open the Pricing page from the website menu to compare plans without logging in. Each plan card shows its price, what is included, and a button to get started.
Billing toggle - switch the prices between Monthly, Quarterly and Yearly. Quarterly and yearly cost less per month than paying monthly.
Plan card - shows the plan name, a short description, the price per month, the total for the chosen cycle, and a note such as Billed every month, Billed every 3 months or Billed annually.
Most Popular - the highlighted plan is the one most schools pick.

What every plan includes - unlimited students, unlimited staff, dashboard access and email support. Plans differ in the number of sub-admins (shown as Up to N sub-admins) and in extra features listed on the card.
Free plan - shows Free and the button Get Started Free. Paid plans show Choose Plan.

steps.desc: Log in as the Super Admin and open Settings from the admin sidebar, then choose Subscriptions (the page title is Settings & Subscriptions). You can also click the upgrade button in the profile menu at the top bar, or the Renew button on the expiry banner.

blocks.text: Log in as the Super Admin and open Settings from the admin sidebar, then choose Subscriptions (the page title is Settings & Subscriptions). You can also click the upgrade button in the profile menu at the top bar, or the Renew button on the expiry banner.
The page has three tabs: Current Plan, Upgrade/Downgrade and Billing History.
Only the Super Admin can renew or change the plan. Other admins and staff see a message asking them to contact the Super Admin.

steps.desc: This tab is your subscription dashboard. It shows the plan you are on, its status and how much of each limit you have used.

blocks.text: This tab is your subscription dashboard. It shows the plan you are on, its status and how much of each limit you have used.
Plan name and status badge - the plan name with a badge such as Active, Cancelled or Expired.
Expiry - the date the subscription expires and the number of days remaining. When it has ended it shows Expired on with the date and Access suspended.
Sub-Admins - used / allowed, with a progress bar. The bar is green under 75%, amber from 75% and red from 90%.
Storage - used / allowed in the plan's unit, with the same colour-coded progress bar.
Included Features - a checklist of everything your plan gives you.
Upgrade Plan - takes you to the Upgrade/Downgrade tab.
View Billing History - takes you to the Billing History tab.
Cancel Subscription - visible while the plan is active. See the cancel step below.

steps.desc: This tab lists every available plan as a card so you can switch plan or renew the current one.

blocks.text: This tab lists every available plan as a card so you can switch plan or renew the current one.
Expiring soon warning - when 7 days or fewer remain, a banner shows the expiry date and days left so you can renew before access is interrupted.
View Prices By - choose Monthly, Quarterly or Yearly to change the prices shown on all cards.
Plan card - shows the plan name, description, price, Unlimited students, Unlimited staff, Up to N sub-admins, Dashboard access, Email support and the plan's extra features.

Card badges and buttons - the plan you are on shows Current Plan with a disabled button. If your subscription has ended, that card shows Renew instead. Other paid plans show Upgrade, or Downgrade if the plan is lower than your current one. The free plan has no purchase button.

steps.desc: Click Upgrade, Downgrade or Renew on a plan card. A panel slides in to confirm the change and take payment.

blocks.text: Click Upgrade, Downgrade or Renew on a plan card. A panel slides in to confirm the change and take payment.
Plan comparison - your Current Plan on the left and the New Plan on the right, with unlimited students, unlimited staff and the sub-admin limit for each.
What you'll get - highlights such as more sub-admins (with how many extra), more storage and priority support.
Billing Cycle - Monthly, Quarterly or Yearly. Quarterly and yearly are discounted.

steps.step: When your subscription expires or is cancelled

Super Admin - the banner has a Renew button that opens the Upgrade/Downgrade tab.
Other admins and staff - the banner says Ask your Super Admin to renew.

Students do not see the banner.
After a successful renewal, access is restored immediately without logging out.

blocks.text: Every school runs on a subscription plan. Plans control how many sub-admins you can add, how much file storage you get, and paid extras such as a hosted school website. Students and staff are unlimited on every plan. This guide shows where to manage your plan, what each screen contains, how to pay, and what happens when a subscription ends.

items.title: Session Management
items.content: A session is one full school year, and terms (also called subsessions) are the parts of that year, such as First, Second and Third Term. This guide explains how to create and manage sessions and terms, and, most importantly, how a session and a term become active. Everything in the school (student admission, the dashboard, report cards, timetables, events) follows the active session and the active term. Required fields are marked with *.

steps.step: The big idea: sessions and terms
steps.desc: A session covers the whole academic year with a start date and an end date. Inside it you create terms, each with its own start and end date. There is no button to start or activate a session. Its status is worked out automatically from today's date.

blocks.text: A session covers the whole academic year with a start date and an end date. Inside it you create terms, each with its own start and end date. There is no button to start or activate a session. Its status is worked out automatically from today's date.
Session = the full year, for example 2025/2026 from 8 September 2025 to 24 July 2026.
Term (subsession) = a part of the year, for example First Term from 8 September to 19 December.
Terms must sit inside their session's dates, and two terms cannot overlap.
Students, classes, scores, timetables, events and report cards all work inside a session and a term.

steps.desc: The system compares today's date with the session's start and end dates every time the page loads. Nobody has to switch it on or off.

blocks.text: The system compares today's date with the session's start and end dates every time the page loads. Nobody has to switch it on or off.
Draft - today is before the start date. The session has not started yet (it is an upcoming session).
Active - today is on or after the start date and on or before the end date. Both the start day and the end day count as active.
Completed - today is after the end date. The year is over.
Archived - you archived it. An archived session is never active, even if today is inside its dates, until you reactivate it.
Example: a session from 8 Sep 2025 to 24 Jul 2026 is Draft until 7 Sep 2025, Active from 8 Sep 2025 to 24 Jul 2026, and Completed from 25 Jul 2026.
So to make a session active you do not click anything. You either wait for its start date, or you set the dates so that today falls inside them (see Edit a session).

steps.desc: Terms follow exactly the same rule, using the term's own start and end dates.

blocks.text: Terms follow exactly the same rule, using the term's own start and end dates.
Draft - the term has not started yet.
Active - today is inside the term's start and end dates (both days included).
Completed - the term's end date has passed.
Only one term can be active at a time, because terms cannot overlap.
The term status badge shows on every term card in the session overview, and a small green dot marks the active term in the left sidebar.

steps.step: The holiday gap: active session but no active term
steps.desc: Between terms there is usually a holiday. During that time the session is still Active, but no term is.

blocks.text: Between terms there is usually a holiday. During that time the session is still Active, but no term is.
Example: First Term ends 19 Dec and Second Term starts 12 Jan. From 20 Dec to 11 Jan the session is Active and there is no active term.

In that period the dashboard shows the session with No active term, and the Add Student form says No active term found. The session is active but has no running subsession, and the form stays locked with the message No active term - go to Sessions to create a subsession. Add a term that covers today to unlock it.
The same happens if you forget to create a term for the dates you are in. Add the missing term in the session overview.
Likewise if no session covers today, the dashboard shows No Active Session and the top bar for students and staff shows No active session.

steps.step: Where the active session and term are used
steps.desc: Once a session and term are active, these parts of the app pick them up automatically.

blocks.text: Once a session and term are active, these parts of the app pick them up automatically.
Dashboard - the Academic Session card shows the session name, the active term (or No active term) and a Session Progress bar from the start date to the end date.
Top bar - students, teachers and staff see the active session and active term in a pill at the top of their dashboard.
Add Student - the form shows the Active Session and Active Term and uses them for the new student's enrolment. If there is no active session you must pick a session and a term yourself (see below).
Sidebar - the Sessions area lists every term with the session name, and a green dot marks the active term.
Teacher calendar and events - they show only the current session. Without one they say There is no active session or term for today.
Alumni - actions that need a session show No active session found. if there is none.

steps.step: When there is no active session
steps.desc: If today is outside every session, for example during the long break or before your first session starts, the Add Student form tells you.

blocks.text: If today is outside every session, for example during the long break or before your first session starts, the Add Student form tells you.
No sessions at all - the page says No Session Available and offers Go to Sessions Page. Create a session and at least one term first.

Sessions exist but none is active - the page says No Active Session for Today. It shows your sessions as cards marked Immediate Past or Immediate Upcoming. Click one, then pick a Term / Subsession *, and the form unlocks.
The chosen session has no terms - a warning says This session has no subsessions. Please create subsessions for this session first.

steps.desc: Click Sessions in the admin sidebar (the page is called Academic Sessions). A blue banner at the top reminds you that a session is active when today's date is inside its dates, with a Learn how sessions work link to this guide.

blocks.text: Click Sessions in the admin sidebar (the page is called Academic Sessions). A blue banner at the top reminds you that a session is active when today's date is inside its dates, with a Learn how sessions work link to this guide.
Each session is a card showing its name, code, a status badge (draft, active, completed), the Start Date and End Date, who created it, and View Details.
Search - type a name, code, status (for example draft) or creator. A line shows how many sessions were found, and Clear Search brings the full list back.
View Archived (number) - opens archived sessions. It appears only when you have archived ones and can edit sessions.
Create New Session - a lock icon appears instead of the plus if you do not have permission.
If you have no sessions the page says No Academic Sessions Found.

steps.desc: Click Create New Session. A four-step wizard opens. You move forward with Next, which stays disabled until the step is valid.

blocks.text: Click Create New Session. A four-step wizard opens. You move forward with Next, which stays disabled until the step is valid.
Step 1, Session Basics: Session Name * (for example 2025/2026), Session Code * (must be unique in your school), Start Date * and End Date *.

Date rules: the start must be before the end; the session must last at least 30 days and no more than 2 years; it cannot already be over (the end date must be today or later); and it cannot overlap another session that is not archived. Touching is allowed, so a new session may start on the day another ends.

Step 2, Student Promotion and Graduation (you can click Skip): choose a Promotion Template. The page shows how many students will be promoted, demoted (held back) and graduated. Click a number to see the students and change any one of them to Promote, Demote or Graduate. See Class Promotion Templates.

Step 3, Create Subsessions: three default terms are ready, First Term (TERM1), Second Term (TERM2) and Third Term (TERM3), marked Default. For each fill Start Date, End Date and a Grading Template *. You can rename them, add more terms, or remove a default (you are asked to confirm).
Step 4, Review: check the dates, terms, grading templates and promotion counts, then create.

steps.step: One upcoming session at a time
steps.desc: You can only have one draft (not yet started) session at any time.

blocks.text: You can only have one draft (not yet started) session at any time.
If a draft session already exists, the wizard shows A draft session already exists. You must delete it before creating a new session, and the create button is disabled.
This means you can prepare next year's session in advance, but you must delete that draft before creating a different upcoming one.
Once the draft's start date arrives it becomes Active on its own, and you can then create the next upcoming session.

steps.step: What happens when you create the session
steps.desc: When you click create, everything is saved in one go.

blocks.text: When you click create, everything is saved in one go.
The session and all its terms are created, each with the grading template you chose. A grading template cannot be changed later, so choose carefully.

If you did not skip step 2, student promotions happen immediately, not on the start date. Promoted and held-back students get a class assignment in the new session, and graduating students are moved to Alumni with the session's end date as their graduation date.
You see a message such as Academic session created successfully with 3 subsession(s), 120 student(s) (100 promoted, 10 demoted, 10 graduated).
If something fails you see warnings such as 1 subsession(s) failed to create or 2 student promotion(s) failed, and the rest is still saved.
The new session shows as Draft if it starts in the future, or Active if today is already inside its dates.

steps.desc: Click a session card. The session has four tabs: Overview, Admissions, Students and Promotions, and Graduation.

blocks.text: Click a session card. The session has four tabs: Overview, Admissions, Students and Promotions, and Graduation.
Overview shows three cards - Session Period (name and dates), Total Students (enrolled in this session) and Subsessions (number of terms and how many are archived).
Below is the list of terms, numbered, each with its dates, a status pill (draft, active or completed), its Grading Template and a menu with Edit and Archive (Delete for a draft).
Add Subsession is hidden for a completed session, which instead says This completed session doesn't have any subsessions.

steps.desc: Click Add Subsession to add another term. Use the menu on a term to edit it.

blocks.text: Click Add Subsession to add another term. Use the menu on a term to edit it.
Add Subsession: Subsession Name *, Subsession Code * (unique inside the session), Start Date *, End Date * and a Grading Template (a template is required).

Rules: the dates must be inside the session dates, the start must be before the end, it must not overlap another term (touching is fine), and a term that has already ended cannot be created or changed.
Error messages explain the problem, for example Subsession start date must be within session dates or Dates overlap with First Term.
Edit Subsession changes the name and the dates under the same rules. The status then updates by itself from the new dates.

steps.step: Admissions, Students and Promotions, Graduation tabs
steps.desc: These tabs show what happened to students in this session. They are read-only lists with search, sorting and CSV export.

blocks.text: These tabs show what happened to students in this session. They are read-only lists with search, sorting and CSV export.

Admissions - students admitted in this session. Cards show Active, Inactive and Total. Columns are Student ID, Student Name, Class, Stream, Admitted and Status. Click a row for Assignment ID, Admitted Date, Class, Stream, Session and any remarks.

Students and Promotions - students who were promoted or held back into this session. The Status badge is Promoted, Held Back or New Admission. Columns are Student ID, Student Name, Promoted Class, Stream, Status and Date. The detail panel adds Assignment ID, Session, Active and Remarks.
Graduation - graduates of this session. Columns are Student Name, Admission No., Final Class, Graduation Date, Email and Actions. View Profile opens the student's alumni profile.

steps.step: Term pages: events, calendar, reports and timetables
steps.desc: In the sidebar, click a term to open its pages. Each is limited to that term.

blocks.text: In the sidebar, click a term to open its pages. Each is limited to that term.
School Events - Add Event with Event Title *, Description *, Location *, Category, Organizer and Participants, plus the date and time. Needs the School Event permission for sub-admins.

School Calendar - Add Calendar Item with Title *, Description *, Date *, Time *, Type (Academic, Holiday, Meeting, Examination, Sports or Cultural), Priority (High, Medium or Low), Location, Duration and Participants.
Student Report - Create Report Cards, Publish Report Cards and Send Result Emails for students in bulk, with a Report Card Preview. See Generating Report Cards.
Timetable - Subsession Timetables lists each class. Use AI Generate with an AI Model, a Timetable Template * and optional Notes / Instructions. See Timetable Templates.

steps.desc: Use the three-dot menu on a session card, then Edit. The Edit Session panel has Session Name *, Start Date * and End Date *.

blocks.text: Use the three-dot menu on a session card, then Edit. The Edit Session panel has Session Name *, Start Date * and End Date *.
The start must be before the end, and the end date cannot be in the past.
The new dates cannot overlap another session that is not archived. You see Session dates overlap with existing session followed by its name and code.
All active terms must still fit inside the new dates. If not, the message lists the terms that are outside the new range, so edit those terms first.
Because status comes from the dates, changing the dates can change the status. For example moving the start date to a day in the past makes a Draft session Active straight away.

steps.desc: Use the three-dot menu on the session card for Archive or Delete. The same works for terms.

blocks.text: Use the three-dot menu on the session card for Archive or Delete. The same works for terms.
A Draft session (one that has not started) shows Delete. Deleting it is permanent, because there is no history to keep.
An Active or Completed session shows Archive. It moves to View Archived and is hidden from the main list. You need permission, otherwise you see You do not have permission to archive this session.
View Archived - lists archived sessions with their dates, an Archived on date and Reactivate Session.
Reactivate Session - brings it back, and its status is worked out again from its dates. If it overlaps another session, you are shown the overlapping sessions and asked to archive them first.
Terms work the same way. Reactivating a term fails if its dates are outside the session, and if it overlaps another term you can archive that term and continue.

steps.desc: A typical year looks like this.

blocks.text: A typical year looks like this.
Before the year starts - create the new session as an upcoming Draft, with its three terms, grading templates and student promotions.
On the first day - nothing to do. The session and the first term become Active by themselves.
Holidays between terms - the session stays Active with no active term. Add a new term if one is missing.
After the last day - the session and the last term become Completed. Create next year's session, then archive the old one if you want a cleaner list.

items.callout: Sessions and terms are never switched on manually. Active simply means today's date is inside the start and end dates (both days included). Archived sessions are never active, you can only have one not-yet-started (draft) session at a time, and terms must stay inside their session and never overlap.

This guide explains how to create and manage sessions and terms, and, most importantly, how a session and a term become active. Everything in the school (student admission, the dashboard, report cards, timetables, events) follows the active session and the active term. Required fields are marked with *.

items.title: Adding Students
items.content: There are 3 ways to add a student to your school: (1) approve an online application, (2) create the student manually, or (3) enroll an existing student by their Student ID. All three are done from the Students page, and every student must be placed in a class for the active session and term. There is no bulk CSV import.

steps.step: The 3 ways to add a student
steps.desc: Choose the method that matches how the student reached you.

blocks.text: Choose the method that matches how the student reached you.
Way 1, Application approval - a family applied through your public application form. You review the application and click Admit, and the student form opens already filled in.
Way 2, Manual - you type in all the student details yourself. Use this for walk-in students or when there is no application.
Way 3, Existing student - the student already has a Scladapp Student ID (for example from another school on Scladapp). You search by that ID and enroll them without re-entering their details.

steps.desc: Make sure you have what every method needs, otherwise the form is blocked.

blocks.text: Make sure you have what every method needs, otherwise the form is blocked.
Permission - you need permission to add students. Without it you see You do not have permission to add students.

A session and a term - the add panel shows the Active Session and Active Term at the top. If there is no session at all, you are told to go to the Sessions page and create one (button: Go to Sessions Page). If a session is active but has no running term, create or activate a term first.
No active session today - the panel shows cards for the immediate past and immediate upcoming sessions. Click one, then pick a Term/Subsession *. The form unlocks once both are chosen.
At least one class - every student must be placed in a class, so create your classes first.
Plan limit - if your plan's student limit is reached, a Student Limit message appears with an Upgrade Plan button.

steps.desc: Open Students in the sidebar and click Add Student at the top of the list. A panel slides in showing the two cards for adding by hand: Enroll Existing Student (search by ID) and Create New Student (manually enter all information). Approving an application skips this screen and opens the Create New Student form directly.

blocks.text: Open Students in the sidebar and click Add Student at the top of the list. A panel slides in showing the two cards for adding by hand: Enroll Existing Student (search by ID) and Create New Student (manually enter all information). Approving an application skips this screen and opens the Create New Student form directly.
Use the Back button at the bottom of either form to return to the two cards and choose again.

steps.desc: Use this when a family has applied through your public application form. The applicant's details are copied into the student form so you do not retype them.

blocks.text: Use this when a family has applied through your public application form. The applicant's details are copied into the student form so you do not retype them.

Open Applications in the sidebar. Each row shows the Applicant, the Class they applied for, the Guardian contact, the Status and when it was Submitted. A blue dot marks applications you have not opened yet.
Use the tabs All, Pending, Approved and Rejected to filter the list.
Click a row to open the application. It shows everything the family submitted, with the status pill at the top.
At the bottom of the panel you have the actions: Admit (hidden once approved), Reject (hidden once rejected) and Back to pending (hidden while pending).
Click Admit. You are taken to the Students page, the Create New Student form opens, and a message says Application data loaded. Review and complete admission.

Pre-filled fields - full name, date of birth, gender, email (or the guardian email if none), phone, WhatsApp, religion, nationality, state of origin, LGA of origin, place of birth, tribe, NIN, number of siblings, position in the family, lives with, blood group, genotype, residence details, emergency contact and the passport photo. The first guardian is filled in as Primary, and a second guardian is added if the family gave one.
Class - the class the family applied for is selected automatically when its name matches one of your classes. If it does not match, choose the class yourself.
Check every field, fix anything wrong, then save. When the student is created, the application is marked Approved automatically.
Applications only appear once you have turned on Accept new applications and shared your public application link. See the Student Application Form topic for setup.

steps.desc: Click the Create New Student card and fill in the form. Fields marked * are required.

blocks.text: Click the Create New Student card and fill in the form. Fields marked * are required.
Create New Student, Basic Information: Photo (JPEG, PNG or WebP, under 5MB), Full Name *, Date of Birth *, Gender * (Male or Female), Email, Phone, WhatsApp number and Select Class *.

Identity / bio: Religion, Nationality, State of Origin, LGA of origin, Place of birth, Tribe / ethnic group, National Identification Number (NIN), Number of siblings, Position in the family, Lives with (Both parents, Father, Mother, Guardian, Single parent or Orphan), Blood Group and Genotype.
Residence: House number / street, Area / estate, City, LGA of residence, State of residence and Landmark.

Guardian Information: at least one guardian is required. For each guardian fill Guardian Name *, Relationship, Guardian Phone *, Guardian WhatsApp number, Guardian Email, Guardian Occupation and Guardian Address. Click Add Guardian for more, and mark exactly one as Primary.
Emergency Contact: Name, Relationship, Phone and WhatsApp number.
Security and Access: a secure link is emailed so the student or guardian can set a password. It expires after 48 hours. If you leave the student email empty, a temporary placeholder address is used.

Validation - you will be stopped with a message if a required field is empty, if no guardian has both a name and a phone number, if no primary guardian is selected, if no class is chosen, or if the student or guardian email is not a valid email address.
Click the create button at the bottom. A success message confirms the student was created and that a password setup email was sent.

steps.step: Way 3: Enroll an existing student by ID
steps.desc: Use this when the student already exists on Scladapp, for example a transfer from another school. You do not retype their details.

blocks.text: Use this when the student already exists on Scladapp, for example a transfer from another school. You do not retype their details.
Click the Enroll Existing Student card.
Student ID * - type the Student ID and click Search Student.
If the student is not found you see Student not found. If they already have an active admission in your school you see a message that they are already enrolled, and nothing is shown.

If found, a Student Found card with the badge Ready to Enroll shows their Full Name, Student ID, Date of Birth with age, Gender, Guardian, Relationship, Phone, Email, Home Address, Emergency Contact and Permitted Pickup.
Select Class * - choose the class to place the student in. You must choose one before you can enroll.
Check the details carefully (a warning reminds you to verify everything), then click Enroll Student.

steps.desc: The panel closes, the Students list refreshes and the new student appears in the table.

blocks.text: The panel closes, the Students list refreshes and the new student appears in the table.
The student (or guardian) receives an email with a secure link to set their own password. The link expires after 48 hours.
The student is enrolled in the class, session and term you selected.
You can open the student's profile at any time to edit details, add or change guardians, and review their class history.
Use the Active and Inactive switch above the list to view current students or those who have left.

items.callout: There is no bulk CSV import. Add students through an application, manually, or by existing Student ID. A class, plus an active session and term, are required before any student can be added.

All three are done from the Students page, and every student must be placed in a class for the active session and term. There is no bulk CSV import.
