items.title: Guardians
items.content: A guardian is the parent or other adult responsible for a student. Guardian details are used to contact families, and each student can have more than one guardian, with one marked as Primary. Guardians are managed from the student's profile.

blocks.text: A guardian is the parent or other adult responsible for a student. Guardian details are used to contact families, and each student can have more than one guardian, with one marked as Primary. Guardians are managed from the student's profile.

steps.desc: Each guardian is stored against one student and has the following details. Name and phone are the only required fields.

blocks.text: Each guardian is stored against one student and has the following details. Name and phone are the only required fields.
Full Name * - the guardian's full name.
Phone Number * - the main contact number, for example +234 801 234 5678.
WhatsApp number - used by the WhatsApp message button.
Relationship - Father, Mother, Uncle, Aunt, Grandparent, Sibling, Guardian or Other.
Email - the guardian's email address.
Occupation and Workplace - what the guardian does and where they work.
Address - the guardian's home address.
Set as Primary Guardian - a checkbox. The primary guardian is shown first and is the main contact for the student.

steps.step: Add guardians when you create a student
steps.desc: Guardians are first entered when you add the student. The Guardian Information section of the Create New Student form requires at least one guardian with a name and a phone number, and exactly one marked Primary.

blocks.text: Guardians are first entered when you add the student. The Guardian Information section of the Create New Student form requires at least one guardian with a name and a phone number, and exactly one marked Primary.
Click Add Guardian to add more guardians. Each appears as its own card (Guardian 1, Guardian 2 and so on).
On each card you can click Set Primary to make that guardian the primary one, or Remove to delete the card. Remove is only available when there is more than one guardian.

Fields on each card: Guardian Name, Relationship, Guardian Phone, Guardian WhatsApp number, Guardian Email, Guardian Occupation and Guardian Address. If a guardian email is typed it must be a valid email address.
When a student is admitted from an application, the first guardian from the application is filled in automatically as Primary, and a second guardian is added if the family supplied one.

steps.desc: To see or change guardians later, open Students in the sidebar, click the student, and choose Guardians from the profile menu (the menu has Identity, Guardians, Health, Resources and Admission History).

blocks.text: To see or change guardians later, open Students in the sidebar, click the student, and choose Guardians from the profile menu (the menu has Identity, Guardians, Health, Resources and Admission History).
The header shows Student Guardians and how many guardians the student has, for example 2 Guardians.

Each guardian is a card with their photo or initials, name, a Primary badge if applicable, relationship, and the details: Phone, WhatsApp number, Email, Occupation, Workplace and Address. Missing details show N/A.
If the student has no guardians the page says No Guardians Found with an Add Guardian button.

steps.step: Add a guardian to an existing student
steps.desc: Click + Add Guardian at the top of the Guardians tab. A panel slides in. Fill in the fields listed above and click Add Guardian.

blocks.text: Click + Add Guardian at the top of the Guardians tab. A panel slides in. Fill in the fields listed above and click Add Guardian.
Full Name * and Phone Number * must be filled, otherwise the Add Guardian button stays disabled and you see Guardian name and phone are required.
Tick Set as Primary Guardian if this person should be the main contact.
On success you see Guardian added successfully! and the new card appears.

steps.desc: On the guardian's card click the three-dot menu and choose Edit. The same panel opens filled with the current details. Change what you need and click Save Changes.

blocks.text: On the guardian's card click the three-dot menu and choose Edit. The same panel opens filled with the current details. Change what you need and click Save Changes.
Name and phone are still required.
To change who is primary, tick or untick Set as Primary Guardian and save.
On success you see Guardian updated successfully!

steps.desc: On the guardian's card click the three-dot menu and choose Delete. A confirmation panel asks Remove this guardian from the student's profile? and shows the guardian's name. Confirm to remove them.

blocks.text: On the guardian's card click the three-dot menu and choose Delete. A confirmation panel asks Remove this guardian from the student's profile? and shows the guardian's name. Confirm to remove them.
Deleting only removes that guardian from this student. It does not delete the student.
Make sure at least one guardian with a phone number remains so the school can still reach the family.

steps.desc: The Guardians tab has quick tools for reaching families and sharing the details.

blocks.text: The Guardians tab has quick tools for reaching families and sharing the details.

WhatsApp button - on each card, opens WhatsApp in a new tab with a ready message: Hello {guardian name}, this is regarding your ward's school matters. If the guardian has no WhatsApp number you see No WhatsApp number available for this guardian, so add one first.

Export PDF - downloads a PDF titled Guardian Information with one card per guardian showing name, Primary badge, relationship, phone, WhatsApp, email and occupation. The file is named after the student.
Print - opens a print-friendly page with every guardian's phone, WhatsApp, email, occupation and address.
Both Export PDF and Print show an error if the student has no guardians yet.

steps.desc: Anyone can open the Guardians tab if they can view the student, but adding, editing and deleting guardians needs permission.

blocks.text: Anyone can open the Guardians tab if they can view the student, but adding, editing and deleting guardians needs permission.
The Super Admin can always add, edit and delete guardians.
A sub-admin needs the Students edit permission. Without it you see messages such as You do not have permission to add guardians.
Guardian details can be updated at any time, so keep them current, especially phone numbers.

items.callout: Every student needs at least one guardian with a name and phone number. Guardian details belong to the individual student, so a family with two children has the guardian recorded on each child.

items.title: Admissions
items.content: An admission is the record that a student has joined a school. It stores the class, session, term, type, admitted date and status, and a student keeps one admission record for every enrollment, so their full school history is always available. A new admission is created every time you add a student (by application, manually, or by existing Student ID).

blocks.text: An admission is the record that a student has joined a school. It stores the class, session, term, type, admitted date and status, and a student keeps one admission record for every enrollment, so their full school history is always available. A new admission is created every time you add a student (by application, manually, or by existing Student ID).

steps.desc: Think of an admission as one line in the student's school history. A student who joins your school, later graduates, and a student who transfers in from another school each have their own admission records.

blocks.text: Think of an admission as one line in the student's school history. A student who joins your school, later graduates, and a student who transfers in from another school each have their own admission records.
Admission ID - a unique ID for the record.
School, Session, Term and Class - where and when the student was admitted.
Type - how the student was admitted, such as new or transfer.
Admitted Date and Close Date - when the admission started and, if it has ended, when it closed.
Previous School, Transfer Certificate and Remarks - extra notes, shown only when they exist.
Status - Active, Graduated, Closed or Inactive (explained below).

steps.desc: You do not create admissions on their own. An admission is created automatically when you add a student to the school.

blocks.text: You do not create admissions on their own. An admission is created automatically when you add a student to the school.
Application approval - admitting an applicant creates the student and their admission.
Manual - creating a new student with the Create New Student form creates the student and their admission in the class, session and term you chose.

Existing student - enrolling a student by Student ID creates a new admission in your school without re-entering their details. If the student already has an active admission in your school you are told they are already enrolled.
See the Adding Students topic for the full steps of each method.

steps.desc: Every admission shows one status badge.

blocks.text: Every admission shows one status badge.
Active - the student is currently enrolled.
Graduated - the student completed their education and was graduated.
Closed - the admission has ended and has a close date.
Inactive - the admission is not active and has no close date.
A graduated admission is always shown as Graduated, even if it is no longer active.

steps.desc: Open Students, click a student, and choose Admission History from the profile menu. This lists every admission the student has had, including at other schools on Scladapp.

blocks.text: Open Students, click a student, and choose Admission History from the profile menu. This lists every admission the student has had, including at other schools on Scladapp.
The header shows the number of admissions, for example 2 admissions, or No records found.

Each card shows the school logo and name, the admission Type, the Term, the status badge, the Class, the first part of the Admission ID, the Admitted date, and either the Closed date or how many years the student has been enrolled (Duration).
Click a card or View details to see everything about that admission.
If the student has no records, the page says No Admission Records.

steps.desc: Clicking a card opens a panel with the full record, split into sections.

blocks.text: Clicking a card opens a panel with the full record, split into sections.
Admission Details - School, Session, Term, Class, Type, Admitted Date, Close Date, Status and Admission ID.
Graduation - shown for graduated students: Graduated ID and Graduation Session.
Additional Information - Previous School, Transfer Certificate and Remarks, shown only when filled.
System - Created By, Created At and Updated At, so you can see who created the record and when.

steps.desc: Use the buttons at the top right of the Admission History tab to share the record, for example for a transfer or a school report.

blocks.text: Use the buttons at the top right of the Admission History tab to share the record, for example for a transfer or a school report.
Export PDF - downloads a file named after the student with one card per admission showing session, type, term, status, class, admitted date and closed date.
Print - opens a print-friendly page with the same details and a coloured status badge.
Both show an error if there are no records.

steps.step: View all admissions in a session
steps.desc: To see every student admitted in one academic session, open Sessions, click the session, and choose Admissions in the session menu (the other tabs are Overview, Students and Promotions, and Graduation).

blocks.text: To see every student admitted in one academic session, open Sessions, click the session, and choose Admissions in the session menu (the other tabs are Overview, Students and Promotions, and Graduation).
Summary cards - Active, Inactive and Total admissions for the session.
Table columns - Student ID, Student Name, Class, Stream, Admitted date and Status (a green Active or grey Inactive pill).
Search the table by student name or ID.
Export - download the list (Student ID, Student Name, Class, Stream, Admitted, Status) for records or reporting.
Click any row to open a panel with the student's name and ID, status, Assignment ID, Admitted Date, Class, Stream, Session and any Remarks.
Sub-admins need access to the Academic Sessions module to open this tab.

items.callout: Admissions are the permanent school history of a student. They are created when a student is added, they carry over if the student moves between schools on Scladapp, and they show whether the student is active, graduated or has left.

items.title: Managing Staff
items.content: Staff are everyone who works at your school: teachers, bursars, secretaries, security and so on. Every staff member has a profile, a portal login, documents, resources and a performance record. Staff can also be turned into teachers or promoted to sub-admins. This guide covers the whole staff life cycle. Required fields are marked with *.

steps.desc: Click Staff in the admin sidebar. The Staff page shows everyone in a table.

blocks.text: Click Staff in the admin sidebar. The Staff page shows everyone in a table.
Table columns - ID, Photo, Name, Email, Position, Job Title, Phone and Status.
Active Staff / Inactive Staff switch - above the table, switch between current staff and staff who are no longer active.
Search and select - search the table, and tick rows to delete several staff members at once. A message tells you how many were deleted and how many failed.
Click a row to open that staff member's profile.
Add Staff button - opens the form to create a new staff member. If you do not have permission you see You do not have permission to add staff.

steps.desc: Click Add Staff. A panel titled Create New Staff Member slides in. Only five fields are required; the rest can be added later by editing the profile.

blocks.text: Click Add Staff. A panel titled Create New Staff Member slides in. Only five fields are required; the rest can be added later by editing the profile.
Personal Information: Staff Photo, Full Name *, Email Address *, Phone Number *, WhatsApp number, Date of Birth and Gender (Male, Female or Other).
Identity / bio: Religion, Marital Status (Single, Married, Divorced or Widowed), Nationality, State of Origin, LGA of origin, Place of birth, Tribe / ethnic group, NIN, Blood Group and Genotype.
Residence: House number / street, Area / estate, City, LGA of residence, State of residence and Landmark.

Employment Information: Position * (for example Principal, Bursar), Department * (for example Administration, Finance), Qualification (for example M.Ed, B.Sc), Years of Experience, Employment Type (Full-time, Part-time, Contract or Temporary) and Joining Date.
Emergency Contact: Name, Relationship, Phone and WhatsApp number.
Security and Access: you do not type a password. After you click Create Staff Member, a secure link is emailed to the staff member so they can set their own password. The link expires after 48 hours.
If your plan's staff limit is reached, a Staff Limit Reached message appears with an upgrade button.

steps.desc: Click a staff member to open their profile. The left card shows their photo, name, status (Active or Inactive) and details, and the tabs across the top let you manage everything about them.

blocks.text: Click a staff member to open their profile. The left card shows their photo, name, status (Active or Inactive) and details, and the tabs across the top let you manage everything about them.

Info card sections - Staff Information (Full Name, Staff ID, Position, Department, Date of Birth, Gender, Email, Phone, WhatsApp, Religion, Marital Status, Nationality), Identity / bio, Residence, Employment and Emergency Contact.
Tabs - Identity, Credentials, Resources, Assignments, Activity and Performance.
Edit Staff button - at the top, opens the same form to update any detail.
Actions menu on the card - Edit Staff Profile, Resend Invite Link, Deactivate Staff (or Activate Staff if inactive), Export PDF and Print.
Only the Super Admin, or a sub-admin with Staff edit permission, can edit staff.

steps.desc: If a staff member never received their email or the link expired, open the Actions menu on their profile and choose Resend Invite Link.

blocks.text: If a staff member never received their email or the link expired, open the Actions menu on their profile and choose Resend Invite Link.

The panel explains what happens: the previous invite link is immediately invalidated, a new secure link is sent to their email, the new link expires in 48 hours, and the staff member sets their own password through it.
The email address it will be sent to is shown under Sending to. Click Send Invite Link to confirm.
If the email address was wrong, edit the profile first, then resend.

steps.step: Deactivate or activate a staff member
steps.desc: Use Actions, then Deactivate Staff to stop someone's access without losing their records. This is reversible.

blocks.text: Use Actions, then Deactivate Staff to stop someone's access without losing their records. This is reversible.
Deactivating prevents the staff member from logging in, removes their access to staff resources and materials, hides them from active staff lists, and keeps all their historical data and records.
To bring them back, open an inactive staff member (use the Inactive Staff switch) and choose Activate Staff, then confirm.
You will see a message such as Staff record deactivated successfully or activated successfully.

steps.desc: The Credentials tab (Credentials & Documents) stores certificates, licences and other documents for the staff member.

blocks.text: The Credentials tab (Credentials & Documents) stores certificates, licences and other documents for the staff member.
Click Upload Document and drag a file in or click to browse.

Document Title * (for example Teaching License 2024), Category (Academic, Administrative, Certification, License, Medical, Legal, Financial, Identity, Training or General), Issuer * (for example Ministry of Education), Document Number, Expiry Date, Verification Status (Pending, Verified, Rejected or Expired), Required Document checkbox, and an optional Description.
Search by name, category, issuer or document number, and filter by file type with the tabs above the list.

Each document card has Download, Delete and View Details. The details panel shows Document Information (title, file name, file type, size, category, document number), Status and Verification (status, verification status, issuer, upload date, expiry date, required, downloads) and the description. From there you can Edit Document.
Deleting asks for confirmation because it cannot be undone.

steps.desc: The Resources tab holds general files for the staff member, such as handbooks or training material.

blocks.text: The Resources tab holds general files for the staff member, such as handbooks or training material.
Click the upload button, then enter Resource Name * (for example School Administration Handbook), Category (for example Administration, Training, Finance) and a Description.
Allowed files - PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX, PPT, PPTX, ZIP and images.
Search by name or category and filter by file type. You can edit or delete a resource later.
If your plan's storage is full, a Storage Limit Reached message appears with an upgrade button.

steps.desc: The Assignments tab shows every role this staff member holds. Click a row for the full record.

blocks.text: The Assignments tab shows every role this staff member holds. Click a row for the full record.
Type - Teacher, Admin or Class assignment (headmaster of a class), with a status of Active or Inactive.
Teacher assignment shows Teacher ID, Teacher Code, Status, Appointed At and Revoked At.
Admin assignment shows Admin ID, Admin Role, Access Scope, Status, Assigned At and Revoked At.
Class assignment shows Assignment ID, Class, Class Code, Status, Start Date and End Date (Ongoing if still active).

steps.desc: The Activity tab is an audit trail of actions performed by this staff member.

blocks.text: The Activity tab is an audit trail of actions performed by this staff member.
Table columns - Action, Category, Status and Date and Time.
Click a row to see Log ID, Action, Category, Status, Performed At and a Description.
Use it to check who changed what and when.

steps.desc: Record formal evaluations for a staff member. Click New Evaluation (or edit an existing one).

blocks.text: Record formal evaluations for a staff member. Click New Evaluation (or edit an existing one).
Evaluation Type * (for example Annual Review), Evaluation Period (for example 2024-2025), Evaluator Name *, Evaluator Role, Evaluation Date *.
Status - Scheduled, In Progress, Completed or Overdue.
Overall Rating - Outstanding, Excellent, Very Good, Good, Satisfactory or Needs Improvement.
Category Ratings - add categories such as Leadership. For each one enter a Score (0-5), a Rating and Comments.
Strengths, Areas for Improvement and Goals - add each point by typing it and pressing Enter or Add.
Overall Comments - free text about the evaluation.
Opening an evaluation shows the overview, category ratings, strengths, improvement areas and goals. You need Staff edit permission to create or edit evaluations.

steps.step: Promote a staff member to sub-admin
steps.desc: A sub-admin is a staff member who can manage parts of the school dashboard. Open Admins in the school directory and click Promote Staff.

blocks.text: A sub-admin is a staff member who can manage parts of the school dashboard. Open Admins in the school directory and click Promote Staff.
The Admins list shows ID, Photo, Name, Email, Admin Role, Access Scope, Position, Phone and Status, with Active Admins and Inactive Admins views.
Select Staff Member - search for the person you want to promote.
Admin Role * - the title, for example Sub Admin or Department Head.
Access Scope * - Limited Access or Full Access. Full Access gives all permissions automatically.
Enable Two-Factor Authentication - requires an OTP code at login for this admin.

Permissions and Access Rights - for each module tick Read, Create, Edit and Delete. Modules are Academic Sessions, School Event, School Calendar, Student Reports, Students, Applications, Classes, Teachers, Staff, Subject, Communication, Bill Income and Expenses, School Account, Report Template, Fee Billing Template, Timetable Template, Announcement Template, Class Promotion Template and Graduate. Read is switched on automatically when you tick Create, Edit or Delete.
Click Promote. You see Staff promoted to Administrator!
Your plan limits how many sub-admins you can have. At the limit you see Sub-Admin Limit Reached with an upgrade button.

items.callout: Deactivating a staff member keeps all their history. Sub-admin count is limited by your plan, while students and staff headcount are unlimited on all plans.

blocks.text: Staff are everyone who works at your school: teachers, bursars, secretaries, security and so on. Every staff member has a profile, a portal login, documents, resources and a performance record. Staff can also be turned into teachers or promoted to sub-admins. This guide covers the whole staff life cycle. Required fields are marked with *.

items.title: Teachers & Subject Assignment
items.content: A teacher is a staff member who has been given a Teacher Code and can be assigned to subjects and classes. Teachers can enter scores, mark attendance and use class resources only for the subjects and classes assigned to them. This guide shows how to create teachers, link them to subjects and classes, make them class headmasters, and review the history. Required fields are marked with *.

steps.desc: Teachers are created from existing staff, and subjects are linked to classes, so set these up first.

blocks.text: Teachers are created from existing staff, and subjects are linked to classes, so set these up first.
Add the person as a staff member first (see Managing Staff).
Create your classes (see Class and Session Setup).
Then create teachers, subjects and assignments in the order below.

steps.desc: Click Teachers in the sidebar to see every teacher.

blocks.text: Click Teachers in the sidebar to see every teacher.
Table columns - ID, Code, Teacher Name, Email, Appointed At, Appointed By and Status.
Active Teachers / Inactive Teachers switch - view current teachers or those who are no longer active.
Click a row to open the teacher's profile. You can also delete several teachers at once.
Add Teacher button - opens the create panel. You need permission, otherwise you see You do not have permission to add teachers.

steps.desc: Click Add Teacher and fill in two fields.

blocks.text: Click Add Teacher and fill in two fields.
Teacher Code * - a unique ID such as TCH001. It identifies the teacher across the system.
Select Staff Member * - search by name, email or department. Staff who are already teachers are hidden.
A preview card shows the selected staff member's staff ID, email, position and department so you can confirm you chose the right person.
Click create. You see Teacher created successfully!
If no staff appear, add staff first or check that they are not already teachers.

steps.desc: Open a teacher to see their profile. The card shows their details and the tabs let you manage assignments.

blocks.text: Open a teacher to see their profile. The card shows their details and the tabs let you manage assignments.
Tabs - Activity, Identity, Resources and Assigned Subjects.
Info card sections - Teacher Information, Staff Profile (with a link to their full staff profile) and Appointment Information.
Actions menu - View Previous Assignments, Change Assignment, Deactivate Teacher (or Reactivate Teacher) and Print.

Change Assignment - lets you point the teacher record to a different staff member. A panel titled Change Staff Assignment asks you to pick the new staff member, and the old one is kept in the history.
View Previous Assignments - shows Previous Staff Assignments, listing each Changed from and Changed to.

steps.desc: Open the teacher and go to the Assigned Subjects tab. This lists every subject the teacher teaches, with Subject, Class, Start Date, Status and Actions.

blocks.text: Open the teacher and go to the Assigned Subjects tab. This lists every subject the teacher teaches, with Subject, Class, Start Date, Status and Actions.
Click Assign Subject. A panel opens with a search box (search by name, code or class).
Pick a subject. A Selected Subject preview shows its name, code and class. If the subject has no class yet, it says No class assigned to this subject yet, so link the subject to a class first.
Click assign. You see Subject assigned successfully. Subjects already assigned to this teacher are not shown again.
A teacher can teach many subjects across many classes.
You need permission to assign. Without it you see No permission to assign subjects.

steps.step: Deactivate or review a subject assignment
steps.desc: When a teacher stops teaching a subject, deactivate the assignment instead of deleting it.

blocks.text: When a teacher stops teaching a subject, deactivate the assignment instead of deleting it.
On the assignment row open the menu and choose View or Deactivate.
Deactivating marks the assignment inactive, sets today as the end date, moves it to assignment history and preserves all historical data. You see Assignment deactivated.
Click History to see Assignment History, which lists inactive subject assignments with Start Date and End Date. From there you can delete an old record permanently.

steps.step: Assign teachers from the subject side
steps.desc: You can also assign from the subject. Open Subjects, click a subject, and use its Teachers and Classes tabs.

blocks.text: You can also assign from the subject. Open Subjects, click a subject, and use its Teachers and Classes tabs.
The Subject profile has tabs Overview, Classes, Teachers, Books, Resources and Assessments.
Classes tab - link the subject to classes. Choose a class and assign it. You can deactivate, restore or delete class assignments.
Teachers tab - assign a teacher by choosing the teacher (shown as name and code) and an active class. The tab also warns you about classes that have no active teacher.
Each teacher assignment can be deactivated, reactivated or deleted. You need the matching permission or you see messages such as You do not have permission to deactivate teacher assignments.

When you create a subject you can also link classes and teachers in the same form: Subject Name *, Subject Code *, Description, Stream * (Science, Arts, Commercial or General) and Class and Teacher Assignments, where every row needs a Class * and a Teacher *.

steps.desc: The headmaster of a class is the teacher responsible for that class, including attendance and remarks. Open Classes, click the class and go to the Headmaster tab.

blocks.text: The headmaster of a class is the teacher responsible for that class, including attendance and remarks. Open Classes, click the class and go to the Headmaster tab.
If there is no headmaster the page says No Active Headmaster. Click the assign button.
Assign New Headmaster panel - Select Teacher (search and pick), then Assignment Reason / Notes * explaining the change.
The active headmaster card shows name, email, phone, gender, employment type, Assigned date, End Date (Ongoing), Assigned By and Joining Date, with a button to open the teacher's profile.
Assignment History lists previous headmasters, marked Inactive.
You can also set a headmaster when you create the class, or during the Create Session wizard.

steps.desc: Open the teacher's profile, choose Actions, then Deactivate Teacher. This can be reversed later.

blocks.text: Open the teacher's profile, choose Actions, then Deactivate Teacher. This can be reversed later.
Deactivating prevents the teacher from logging in, removes access to teaching materials and classes, hides them from active lists and keeps all historical data.
To restore, use the Inactive Teachers switch, open the teacher and choose Reactivate Teacher.
You see Teacher deactivated successfully or Teacher reactivated successfully.

items.callout: Teachers only see scores, attendance and class resources for the subjects and classes assigned to them. Deactivating an assignment keeps its history, so past records stay accurate.

blocks.text: A teacher is a staff member who has been given a Teacher Code and can be assigned to subjects and classes. Teachers can enter scores, mark attendance and use class resources only for the subjects and classes assigned to them. This guide shows how to create teachers, link them to subjects and classes, make them class headmasters, and review the history. Required fields are marked with *.

items.title: Class & Session Setup
items.content: Sessions and terms (subsessions) define your academic calendar. Classes organise students, and subjects, teachers, timetables and attendance are all managed per class. This guide covers creating and managing sessions and terms first, then classes and everything inside a class profile. Required fields are marked with *.

steps.desc: Click Sessions in the sidebar. Each session is a card showing its name, start date, end date and status.

blocks.text: Click Sessions in the sidebar. Each session is a card showing its name, start date, end date and status.
Statuses - Draft (not started), Active (today is inside its dates), Completed (end date passed) and Archived. Status follows the dates automatically; see Session Management.
Search by name, code, status or creator using the box at the top.
If you have no sessions yet the page says No Academic Sessions Found and invites you to create your first one.
Click a card to open the session overview with its terms.

steps.desc: Click the create button to open the Create New Academic Session wizard. It has four steps and Next stays disabled until the current step is valid.

blocks.text: Click the create button to open the Create New Academic Session wizard. It has four steps and Next stays disabled until the current step is valid.
Step 1, Session Basics: Session Name * (for example 2025/2026), Session Code *, Session Start Date * and Session End Date *. The end date must come after the start date.

Step 2, Student Promotion and Graduation (can be skipped for a new school): choose a Promotion Template, then review how many students will be promoted, demoted or graduated. Click a card to change any student's status to Promote, Demote or Graduate.

Step 3, Create Subsessions (terms): for each term enter Subsession Name * (for example First Term), Term Code * (for example TERM1), Start Date *, End Date * and a Grading Template *. The grading template is required and cannot be changed later.
Step 4, Review: check the session name, duration, promotion template and each term, then create.
Make your Class Promotion template and Grading template before you start (see Setting up your school).

steps.step: Edit, archive or delete a session
steps.desc: Use the buttons on the session card to manage it.

blocks.text: Use the buttons on the session card to manage it.
Edit - opens Edit Session with Session Name *, Start Date * and End Date *. Start must be before end, or you see Start date must be before end date.

Archive - moves a session out of the main list. A draft session (one that has not started yet) is deleted instead of archived. Archiving needs permission, otherwise you see You do not have permission to archive this session.
Archived - opens Archived Sessions, a list of every archived session for the school.
Reactivate - restores an archived session, and its status is then worked out again from its dates. If it overlaps another session you are asked to archive the overlapping session first.

steps.desc: Open a session to see its terms. Terms are the periods such as First Term, Second Term and Third Term.

blocks.text: Open a session to see its terms. Terms are the periods such as First Term, Second Term and Third Term.
Add subsession panel - Subsession Name *, Subsession Code *, Start Date *, End Date * and a Template (required; you will see A template is required if it is missing). All fields are required.

Terms must fall inside the session's start and end dates, and they cannot overlap another active term. You will see messages such as Subsession dates must be within session date range or Dates overlap with First Term.
A term's status comes from its dates: draft before it starts, active while today is inside its dates, completed after the end date.
Edit a term to change its name, code or dates, subject to the same rules.
Archive a term to retire it. A draft term is deleted instead.
Reactivate an archived term - its status is worked out again from its dates. If its dates overlap another term, you are offered to archive the overlapping term and continue.
Only one term is normally running at a time, and students are enrolled into the active term.

steps.desc: Open Classes in the sidebar and click Add Class. Create one class for each group of students, such as JSS 1 A and JSS 1 B.

blocks.text: Open Classes in the sidebar and click Add Class. Create one class for each group of students, such as JSS 1 A and JSS 1 B.
Class Name * - for example Grade 10 Science.
Class Code * - for example G10-SCI-A.
Class Section * - Section A, B, C, D or E.
Class Type * - Regular, Advanced, Honors, Remedial or Special.
Room Number - for example Room 101.
Class Teacher (Headmaster) - optional; search and pick a teacher.
The list shows ID, Code, Class Name, Class Teacher, Students, Room and Status, with Active Classes and Inactive Classes views. You can delete several classes at once.

steps.desc: Click a class to open its profile. The Overview tab shows the class details and headmaster.

blocks.text: Click a class to open its profile. The Overview tab shows the class details and headmaster.
Tabs - Students, Timetable and Attendance (shown for each term), and Overview, Resources, Subjects and Headmaster.
Basic Information - Class Name, Class Code, Section, Class Type, Room Number, Status, Class ID and Created date.
Class Headmaster - Headmaster Name, Email, Assignment Start and Assignment End.
Actions - Edit, Export PDF, Print and Deactivate Class (or Activate Class).
Deactivating makes the class inactive, hides it from active class lists, prevents new student enrollments and keeps all historical data.

steps.desc: The Subjects tab lists every subject taught in this class with its teacher.

blocks.text: The Subjects tab lists every subject taught in this class with its teacher.
Columns - Subject, Description, Teacher, Teacher Email, Status and Actions.

Add Subject - opens the subject form with this class already selected: Subject Name *, Subject Code *, Description, Stream, and Teacher. The subject is created, linked to the class and assigned to the teacher.
Row actions - View (subject details with teacher name, email and phone) and Deactivate.
History - shows inactive subject assignments for this class with their start and end dates. You can Restore an assignment or Delete the record.

steps.step: Class profile: students, attendance and timetable
steps.desc: These tabs are shown per term, so choose the term you are working in.

blocks.text: These tabs are shown per term, so choose the term you are working in.
Students - lists the students in the class for that term with Student, Admission No., Gender, Date of Birth, Phone, Guardian, Guardian Phone and Status.
Attendance - click Mark Attendance. Mark each student Present, Absent or Excused, or use mark all to set everyone at once, then save. Marking attendance needs permission.

Timetable - shows the weekly schedule. Click Create Timetable (or Edit Timetable). Add each entry with Day, Start and End times, and choose Subject (pick one or more subjects) or Break / Interval (give it a name such as Morning Break or Lunch). All entries are listed with Edit and Delete.

AI Generate - in the timetable editor, choose a Timetable Template, add optional instructions (for example Science stream in the morning, avoid double periods on Fridays) and the AI builds a timetable for this class. Review it, then save.
Export PDF - download the timetable.

steps.desc: Finish the class setup by naming a headmaster and adding teaching files.

blocks.text: Finish the class setup by naming a headmaster and adding teaching files.
Headmaster - assign a teacher with a reason, as described in the Teachers topic. The history of previous headmasters is kept.
Resources - upload files for the class, such as notes and past papers. If your storage is full you are asked to upgrade.

items.callout: Create classes before subjects and students. A term must exist and be active before students can be enrolled. Deactivating a class or archiving a session never deletes its history.

blocks.text: Sessions and terms (subsessions) define your academic calendar. Classes organise students, and subjects, teachers, timetables and attendance are all managed per class. This guide covers creating and managing sessions and terms first, then classes and everything inside a class profile. Required fields are marked with *.

items.title: School Profile & Settings
items.content: The School page holds your school's identity, files and photos, and the Settings page holds your subscription and system preferences. This guide covers every tab and field. Required fields are marked with *.

steps.desc: Click School in the admin sidebar. The page is titled School (Manage your school profile, bio, resources and gallery) and has three tabs: Profile, Resources and Gallery.

blocks.text: Click School in the admin sidebar. The page is titled School (Manage your school profile, bio, resources and gallery) and has three tabs: Profile, Resources and Gallery.
The Super Admin can edit everything here.

steps.desc: The Profile tab shows your school at a glance.

blocks.text: The Profile tab shows your school at a glance.
The header shows your logo, the school name and an Edit Profile button.
Details shown - School Name, Slogan, Email, Phone, State, Country and Address.
Social - your connected social profiles, or No social profiles added yet.

steps.desc: Click Edit Profile to change anything.

blocks.text: Click Edit Profile to change anything.
School Logo - click to upload a new logo (JPG, PNG or WEBP, maximum 5MB) or Remove the new one before saving.
School Name * - the official name.
School Slogan, Phone Number, Email Address, State and Country.
Address - the full address, in a larger text box.
Click save to apply the changes, or Cancel to discard them.

steps.desc: In the Social section of the edit form you can connect your school's social media.

blocks.text: In the Social section of the edit form you can connect your school's social media.
Choose the platform (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok or LinkedIn) and type the handle, then click Add. If either is missing you see Select a platform and enter a handle.
Each added link appears in the list and can be removed with its remove button.
Save the profile to keep the links.

steps.desc: Store school-wide files here, such as the school handbook, policies and curriculum documents.

blocks.text: Store school-wide files here, such as the school handbook, policies and curriculum documents.
Click Upload Resource and choose a file (PDF, DOC, XLS, PPT, ZIP or images).
Resource Name * (for example School Handbook), Category (for example Policy, Curriculum), Description and Visibility.
Visibility - Public means visible to all students and staff; the other option means only admins and staff can see it.
Search by name or category and filter by file type: all, pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx or zip.
Each resource can be downloaded, edited or deleted. Deleting asks for confirmation.
If your plan's storage limit is reached you see a Storage Limit Reached message with an upgrade button.

steps.desc: Show off school life with photos.

blocks.text: Show off school life with photos.
Click Upload Photos, then select one or more images (JPG, PNG, GIF or WEBP). Previews appear before you upload.
Add a Caption (for example Sports Day 2025) and pick a Category: General, Events, Sports, Academics, Graduation or Facilities.
Search the gallery by caption and filter by category.
Click a photo to open it full size. From there you can Delete it or Close the view.
Photos load 20 per page. Use Prev and Next to move between pages.

steps.desc: Click Settings in the sidebar. The page is titled Settings and Subscriptions and has two tabs: Subscriptions and System Settings.

blocks.text: Click Settings in the sidebar. The page is titled Settings and Subscriptions and has two tabs: Subscriptions and System Settings.
Subscriptions - your plan, upgrades, billing history and cancellation. See the Subscription and Plans topic.
System Settings - has three tabs: Theme, Security and Backup.

steps.desc: Open System Settings, then the Security tab to protect your account.

blocks.text: Open System Settings, then the Security tab to protect your account.

Change Password - enter Current Password *, New Password * (at least 8 characters) and Confirm New Password *. You see messages such as All password fields are required, New passwords do not match and New password must be at least 8 characters if something is wrong, and Password updated successfully on success.
Two-Factor Authentication - tick Enable 2FA for your account to require a verification code at login.

steps.desc: The other two System Settings tabs control how the app looks and data export.

blocks.text: The other two System Settings tabs control how the app looks and data export.
Theme - choose Light Mode (clean and bright), Dark Mode (easy on the eyes in low light) or Auto (System), which follows your device setting. Click a card to select it.
Backup - Full Data Export and Scheduled Backups are shown but marked Coming Soon. They are not available yet.

steps.desc: Two other school-level features have their own guides.

blocks.text: Two other school-level features have their own guides.
School website - request a hosted school website, and edit it with the AI website editor. See the School Website section.
Student applications - turn on the public application form and choose its fields. See the Student Application Form topic.

items.callout: Keep your school profile current. A hosted school website can be requested from the School Website section.

blocks.text: The School page holds your school's identity, files and photos, and the Settings page holds your subscription and system preferences. This guide covers every tab and field. Required fields are marked with *.

items.title: Grading Templates
items.content: A grading template defines how a term's scores are calculated and how the report card looks. It holds the assessment fields (for example First Test, Exam) with their weights, the grading scale (A to F), and the behavioural traits teachers rate. You pick one grading template for every term (subsession) you create. Required fields are marked with *.

blocks.text: A grading template defines how a term's scores are calculated and how the report card looks. It holds the assessment fields (for example First Test, Exam) with their weights, the grading scale (A to F), and the behavioural traits teachers rate. You pick one grading template for every term (subsession) you create. Required fields are marked with *.

steps.desc: Click Templates in the admin sidebar. The Templates page has five tabs across the top: Grading Templates (opens first), Fee Bill Templates, Timetable Templates, Announcement Templates and Class Promotion Templates.

blocks.text: Click Templates in the admin sidebar. The Templates page has five tabs across the top: Grading Templates (opens first), Fee Bill Templates, Timetable Templates, Announcement Templates and Class Promotion Templates.
Each template is a card showing its name, a status badge (active or archived), the description, the number of Fields, Grades and Sections, and the date it was last modified.
If you have none yet the page says No templates found, with a Create Template button.
Sub-admins need the Report Template permission to open this page; Create, Edit and Delete are separate permissions.

steps.desc: Click Create Template. A panel opens titled Create Template (Define grading fields, scheme, and report card layout).

blocks.text: Click Create Template. A panel opens titled Create Template (Define grading fields, scheme, and report card layout).
Template Name * - for example Standard Template.
Description - what this template is for.
A blue note warns you: make sure the data is correct before assigning this template to a subsession, because once it is assigned it cannot be edited or deleted.

steps.desc: The Assessment Fields section lists every score column on the report card. Click Add Field for each one.

blocks.text: The Assessment Fields section lists every score column on the report card. Click Add Field for each one.
Field Name - for example ft (first test), st (second test), Exam.
Weight (%) - how much this field contributes to the final score.
Max Score - the highest mark possible for that field, for example 20 or 60.
The Total shows next to the title and must equal exactly 100%. If not, a warning says Total weight must equal 100% and the Create button stays disabled.
Use the bin icon to remove a field (there must always be at least one).

steps.desc: The Grading Scheme turns the final percentage into a grade. Click Add Grade for each row.

blocks.text: The Grading Scheme turns the final percentage into a grade. Click Add Grade for each row.
Grade - the letter, for example A, B, C.
Min % and Max % - the range of the final score for that grade, for example 70 to 100.
Points - the grade point, for example 5.0 or 4.0.
Pass/Fail - choose Pass or Fail for the grade.

The Total badge shows how much of 0% to 100% your grades cover. It must be 100%. If there are gaps, a warning lists the percentages not covered. If two rows overlap, another warning names the overlapping grades. Fix both before you can save.

steps.desc: Choose the traits teachers will rate on the report card (the Behavioral Traits section).

blocks.text: Choose the traits teachers will rate on the report card (the Behavioral Traits section).

Tap to select from the list: Neatness, Punctuality, Politeness, Honesty, Leadership, Cooperation, Attentiveness, Initiative, Self-Control, Respect for Others, Responsibility, Perseverance, Creativity, Problem Solving, Time Management and Teamwork.
Or type your own trait and click Add (or press Enter).
The selected traits are listed in order and each has a remove button. The counter shows how many are selected. Traits are optional.

steps.step: Save and design the report card
steps.desc: Click Create Template. You see Template created and are taken straight to the visual report card editor, where the report card is generated from your fields, grades and traits.

blocks.text: Click Create Template. You see Template created and are taken straight to the visual report card editor, where the report card is generated from your fields, grades and traits.

The editor has three panels: Template Elements (a tree of every part of the report card) on the left, a live preview in the middle with sample data, and a properties panel on the right for the selected item.
Click anything in the preview or the tree to select it, then change its text, colours, sizes and other properties. In the tree you can delete, duplicate or drag items to reorder them.
Your work auto-saves as a draft every couple of seconds (the badge shows Saving then Draft saved). Click Save (or press Ctrl+S) to publish it.
Undo (Ctrl+Z), Redo (Ctrl+Shift+Z) and Reset are in the top bar. Reset discards your edits and regenerates the original layout.
Use the Templates button at the top left to go back.

steps.step: View, edit, duplicate, deactivate or delete
steps.desc: Click a template card to open its details: assessment fields with the total, the grading scheme, the behavioural traits and a Report Card Preview.

blocks.text: Click a template card to open its details: assessment fields with the total, the grading scheme, the behavioural traits and a Report Card Preview.
Edit Template (inside Report Card Preview) - opens the visual report card editor again.
Pencil icon - edit the name, description, fields, scheme and traits.
Copy icon - Duplicate the template, a quick way to make a variation.
Deactivate or Activate icon - archive a template or bring it back. You are asked to confirm.
Bin icon - Delete (cannot be undone).

steps.step: What changes once a template is assigned
steps.desc: When you pick a template for a term, it becomes assigned and is protected so past results stay correct.

blocks.text: When you pick a template for a term, it becomes assigned and is protected so past results stay correct.
A yellow note says This template is assigned to a subsession. Fields, grading scheme, traits and the name are locked and cannot be deleted.
An assigned template cannot be deactivated or deleted.
To change a locked template, Duplicate it and edit the copy, then use the copy for the next term.

steps.step: Use the template for a term
steps.desc: You choose the grading template when you create a term.

blocks.text: You choose the grading template when you create a term.
In the Create Session wizard (Step 3) or the Add Subsession panel, pick the template under Grading Template *. It is required and cannot be changed later.
Only active templates can be chosen.

items.callout: Weights must add up to 100% and grade ranges must cover 0 to 100% with no overlap. Test your template with Duplicate before assigning it, because an assigned template is locked.

items.title: Timetable Templates
items.content: A timetable template describes the shape of your school day: which days are used, how many periods each day has, start and end times, the longest period, and breaks. The template does not hold subjects. You use it when you generate or build a timetable for a class or term. Required fields are marked with *.

blocks.text: A timetable template describes the shape of your school day: which days are used, how many periods each day has, start and end times, the longest period, and breaks. The template does not hold subjects. You use it when you generate or build a timetable for a class or term. Required fields are marked with *.

steps.desc: Click Templates in the sidebar, then the Timetable Templates tab.

blocks.text: Click Templates in the sidebar, then the Timetable Templates tab.
Each card shows the name, status, description, how many Days per week, the Max period length in minutes and how many Breaks, plus the schedule type and the last modified date.
If you have none the page says No timetable templates found.
Sub-admins need the Timetable Template permission.

steps.desc: Click Create Template. A panel titled Create Timetable Template opens (Configure your timetable structure and layout).

blocks.text: Click Create Template. A panel titled Create Timetable Template opens (Configure your timetable structure and layout).
Template Name * - for example Standard Weekly Timetable.
Schedule Type - Weekly Schedule, Block Schedule, Elementary Schedule, Exam Schedule or Custom Schedule.
Description - what this template is for.

steps.desc: Choose the school days and how many periods each has.

blocks.text: Choose the school days and how many periods each has.
Days per Week - tick any of Monday to Sunday. Monday to Friday are ticked by default.
Periods per Day - a number box for every ticked day (0 to 12, default 8). Each selected day needs at least 1 period.
Max Period Duration (minutes) - the longest a period can be, from 15 to 120 (default 40).

steps.desc: Under Daily Schedule Times, set a Start Time and End Time for every selected day (default 08:00 to 15:00).

blocks.text: Under Daily Schedule Times, set a Start Time and End Time for every selected day (default 08:00 to 15:00).
The end time must be after the start time.
There must be enough time for all periods and breaks: at least 15 minutes per period plus the break time. If not, the error tells you how many minutes you need and how many you have.

steps.desc: Under Break Configuration, click Add Break for each break or interval. One Morning Break is added for you.

blocks.text: Under Break Configuration, click Add Break for each break or interval. One Morning Break is added for you.
Break Name - for example Morning Break or Lunch.
Duration (minutes) - at least 5.
After Period - the break comes after this period number. It cannot come after the last period of a day.
Apply to Days - tick the days this break happens on (at least one).
Remove Break deletes it (shown when there are two or more).

steps.desc: Click Preview to see a sample timetable built from your settings. It uses sample subjects only to show how periods and breaks fall.

blocks.text: Click Preview to see a sample timetable built from your settings. It uses sample subjects only to show how periods and breaks fall.
Any problem (no day selected, bad times, not enough time, break rules) is shown as an error message and the preview is blocked until you fix it.
Click Create Template to save it. You see Timetable template created successfully.

steps.desc: Click a card to see the details: days per week, max period, number of breaks, each day's periods and times, and every break with its duration, position and days.

blocks.text: Click a card to see the details: days per week, max period, number of breaks, each day's periods and times, and every break with its duration, position and days.
Pencil icon - edit the template.
Copy icon - duplicate it.
Bin icon - delete it (you are asked to confirm).
You need the Create, Edit or Delete permission for these actions.

steps.desc: Your templates appear when you build timetables.

blocks.text: Your templates appear when you build timetables.
Class Timetable - in a class's Timetable tab, open the editor and use AI Generate, then pick a Timetable Template and add any instructions.
Term timetable - the admin timetable page for a term also reads your templates.
Keep one template per school-day pattern, for example one for Monday to Friday and one for exam weeks.

items.callout: Timetable templates only define time slots and breaks. Add subjects and teachers when you build each class timetable.

items.title: Fee Bill Templates
items.content: A fee bill template is a ready-made fee structure: a list of items with amounts, a currency, a due-date description and optional instalments. Save your usual bills once, then duplicate and adjust them. Required fields are marked with *.

blocks.text: A fee bill template is a ready-made fee structure: a list of items with amounts, a currency, a due-date description and optional instalments. Save your usual bills once, then duplicate and adjust them. Required fields are marked with *.

steps.desc: Click Templates in the sidebar, then the Fee Bill Templates tab.

blocks.text: Click Templates in the sidebar, then the Fee Bill Templates tab.
Each card shows the name, status, description, Total amount, number of Bill items, the Installments (or Single payment), the first three items with their amounts, and the last modified date.
If you have none the page says No fee bill templates found.
Sub-admins need the Fee Billing Template permission.

steps.desc: Click Create Template. A panel titled Create Fee Bill Template opens.

blocks.text: Click Create Template. A panel titled Create Fee Bill Template opens.
Template Name * - for example Termly Tuition Bill.
Category - fixed to Fees.
Description - for example Standard bill for junior classes.

steps.desc: The Bill Items section lists every charge. Click Add Item for each one.

blocks.text: The Bill Items section lists every charge. Click Add Item for each one.
Item Name - for example Tuition, Books and Supplies, Uniform.
Amount - in the template currency, for example 50000.
Description - a short note, for example Core academic fees.
The Total updates live as you type. It must be more than 0.
Remove an item with the bin icon (there must always be at least one).

steps.desc: The Payment Options section controls how the bill is paid.

blocks.text: The Payment Options section controls how the bill is paid.
Currency - Nigerian Naira (NGN), US Dollar (USD), British Pound (GBP) or Euro (EUR).
Due Date Description - free text, for example 30 days after term start.
Allow Installments - tick to let the bill be paid in parts. Then set Number of Installments (2 to 12) and Minimum Payment, the smallest amount accepted per payment.
If installments are off, the bill is a single payment.

steps.desc: Click Create Template. The button stays disabled until there is a name, at least one item and a total above 0.

blocks.text: Click Create Template. The button stays disabled until there is a name, at least one item and a total above 0.
You see Fee bill template created successfully, and the template appears as an active card.
Error messages you may see: Template name is required, Total amount must be greater than 0 and At least one bill item is required.

steps.step: View, edit, duplicate, deactivate or delete
steps.desc: Click a card to open the details.

blocks.text: Click a card to open the details.
The details show every bill item with its amount and description, the Total Amount, and the Payment Configuration (currency, due date, installments and minimum payment).
Pencil icon - edit. Copy icon - duplicate. Deactivate or Activate icon - archive or restore (you are asked to confirm). Bin icon - delete (cannot be undone).
You need the Create, Edit or Delete permission for these actions.

steps.desc: A few habits keep your bills tidy.

blocks.text: A few habits keep your bills tidy.
Make one template per class group or fee type, for example Junior Tuition, Senior Tuition and Boarding.
Duplicate last term's template and change amounts instead of starting again.
Deactivate old templates instead of deleting them, so you can bring them back later.

items.callout: Set the currency before you enter amounts. Instalment count must be between 2 and 12 and the minimum payment is the smallest amount accepted per payment.

items.title: Announcement Templates
items.content: An announcement template is a reusable message with a subject line, formatted content and placeholders such as the student's name, plus a branded email layout (header and footer). Create it once and reuse it for fee reminders, event invitations, holiday notices and more. Required fields are marked with *.

blocks.text: An announcement template is a reusable message with a subject line, formatted content and placeholders such as the student's name, plus a branded email layout (header and footer). Create it once and reuse it for fee reminders, event invitations, holiday notices and more. Required fields are marked with *.

steps.desc: Click Templates in the sidebar, then the Announcement Templates tab.

blocks.text: Click Templates in the sidebar, then the Announcement Templates tab.
Each card shows the name, status, description, how many Channels and Placeholders it has, the channel chips, the category and the last modified date.
If you have none the page says No announcement templates found.
Sub-admins need the Announcement Template permission.

steps.desc: Click Create Template. A panel titled Create Announcement Template opens.

blocks.text: Click Create Template. A panel titled Create Announcement Template opens.
Template Name * - for example General School Announcement.
Category - General Announcement, Emergency Alert, Event Invitation, Academic Update, Administrative Notice or Seasonal/Holiday.
Description - what the template is for.

steps.desc: Placeholders are filled in automatically when the announcement is sent.

blocks.text: Placeholders are filled in automatically when the announcement is sent.

Default placeholders - tick any of {school_name}, {date}, {time}, {recipient_name}, {student_name}, {parent_name}, {session}, {subsession}, {subject}, {class}, {section}, {teacher_name}, {grade} and {academic_year}.
Custom placeholders - type a name such as event_name (the braces are added for you) and click Add. Remove a custom one with its bin icon. Default ones can only be unticked.
Every ticked placeholder becomes a button above the subject and content boxes. Click it to insert it where your cursor is.

steps.desc: Write the message itself.

blocks.text: Write the message itself.
Subject Line Template * - for example Important Update from {school_name}.
Announcement Content Template * - a rich text box. The toolbar has Bold, Italic, Underline, H1, H2, H3, Bullet List, Numbered List and Link.
Link - select text, click Link, enter a Label and a URL and click Insert. Click an existing link and use Link again to edit it or Remove Link. Links open in a new tab.
Placeholders you insert in the content appear as blue tags.

steps.desc: Click Preview to see how the email looks with sample data (Greenwood International School, John Smith, Emma Smith, and so on).

blocks.text: Click Preview to see how the email looks with sample data (Greenwood International School, John Smith, Emma Smith, and so on).
Click Create Template to save. All required fields must be filled. The delivery channel is Email by default; SMS, Website Banner and Social Media are shown as unavailable.
After saving a new template you are taken straight to the email layout editor.

steps.desc: The layout editor lets you style the header and footer that surround your message.

blocks.text: The layout editor lets you style the header and footer that surround your message.
Header - the top section. By default it shows your logo, school name, Official School Communication and the subject.
Body - your announcement text, shown between dashed lines. Click it to edit it.
Footer - the bottom section. By default it says Warm regards, your school administration and a note that it is an official communication.

Toolbar - paragraph style (Normal, Heading 1 to 3), Bold, Italic, Underline, Strikethrough, alignment, bullet and numbered lists, text colour and Image upload. When an image is selected you can align it left, centre or right, or float it so text wraps.
Backgrounds - for the header and footer choose a solid colour, or upload a background image and use the slider to darken or lighten it so the text stays readable.
Edit and Preview switch at the top shows the full email. Save Layout (or Ctrl+S) publishes it. Work auto-saves as a draft; Reset restores the default header and footer.

steps.desc: Click a card to see the Content Template, the Available Placeholders and an Announcement Preview.

blocks.text: Click a card to see the Content Template, the Available Placeholders and an Announcement Preview.
The edit icon next to Announcement Preview opens the email layout editor.
The pencil icon at the bottom edits the content, subject, category and placeholders.
Copy icon - duplicate. Bin icon - delete (you are asked to confirm).
You need the Create, Edit or Delete permission for these actions.

items.callout: Only placeholders you tick appear as insert buttons. Use Preview before saving to check the subject and content read well with real names.

items.title: Class Promotion Templates
items.content: A class promotion template says which class students move to at the end of a session, for example JSS 1 A goes to JSS 2 A, and the final class goes to ALUMNI. You pick one when you create a new academic session, and it is used to promote, demote or graduate students. Required fields are marked with *.

blocks.text: A class promotion template says which class students move to at the end of a session, for example JSS 1 A goes to JSS 2 A, and the final class goes to ALUMNI. You pick one when you create a new academic session, and it is used to promote, demote or graduate students. Required fields are marked with *.

steps.desc: Create all your classes first, because the template picks classes from your class list.

blocks.text: Create all your classes first, because the template picks classes from your class list.
Go to Classes and add every class (see Class and Session Setup).
Decide the path for each class: which class it moves up to, and which class is your graduating class.

steps.desc: Click Templates in the sidebar, then the Class Promotion Templates tab.

blocks.text: Click Templates in the sidebar, then the Class Promotion Templates tab.
Each card shows the name, status, description, the number of Class mappings, the Level and the last modified date.
If you have none the page says No promotion templates found.
Sub-admins need the Class Promotion Template permission.

steps.desc: Click Create Template. A panel titled Create Promotion Template opens (Define promotion criteria and advancement policies).

blocks.text: Click Create Template. A panel titled Create Promotion Template opens (Define promotion criteria and advancement policies).
Template Name * - for example Standard Promotion Criteria.
Grade Level - free text such as Elementary, Secondary or All Levels (the default).
Description - what this path is for.

steps.desc: Each rule moves one class to another. Click Add Promotion Rule for every class.

blocks.text: Each rule moves one class to another. Click Add Promotion Rule for every class.
From Class - choose the current class from the searchable list.
To Class - choose the class students move into. Type ALUMNI for graduating students.
The newest rule is added at the top so you can see it without scrolling.
Use the bin icon to remove a rule (shown when there are two or more).
If a class is missing, use the open-in-new-tab icon to create it, then the refresh icon to reload the class list.

steps.desc: Click Create Template. A name and at least one mapping are required.

blocks.text: Click Create Template. A name and at least one mapping are required.
You see Class promotion template created successfully and the template appears as a card.
Messages you may see: Template name is required and At least one class promotion mapping is required.
Make sure every class that has students appears in a rule, including your last class mapped to ALUMNI.

steps.desc: Click a card to open the Promotion Template details.

blocks.text: Click a card to open the Promotion Template details.
It shows the template name, grade level, description, and the Class Promotion Mapping with the number of rules.
Each rule is shown as a numbered step, From class code and name, an arrow, then To class code and name. ALUMNI rules are highlighted.
Pencil icon - edit. Copy icon - duplicate. Bin icon - delete (you are asked to confirm).
You need the Create, Edit or Delete permission for these actions.

steps.step: Use it when creating a session
steps.desc: The template is used in the Create Session wizard.

blocks.text: The template is used in the Create Session wizard.
Step 2, Student Promotion and Graduation - choose your Promotion Template.
The wizard then shows how many students will be promoted, demoted or graduated, and you can change any student's outcome before creating the session.
You can skip this step for a brand new school with no students yet.

items.callout: Map every class that has students, and use ALUMNI for the final class.

items.title: Generating Report Cards
items.content: Report cards are created per student per term (subsession). Scores and trait ratings can be entered first; then an admin creates the report card, adds remarks, publishes it, and optionally emails a download link. Open a term and go to Student Report, or open a student profile and use the Report tab.

steps.step: Set up the grading template first
steps.desc: A report card uses the grading template assigned to the school: assessment fields (each with a max score), the grading scheme (letter grades with min/max percentage ranges), behavioural traits, and the visual report layout. Create and assign that template under Templates → Grading before you generate reports. If no template is assigned, scores have nowhere to land and the preview has no layout.

blocks.text: A report card uses the grading template assigned to the school: assessment fields (each with a max score), the grading scheme (letter grades with min/max percentage ranges), behavioural traits, and the visual report layout. Create and assign that template under Templates → Grading before you generate reports. If no template is assigned, scores have nowhere to land and the preview has no layout.

steps.step: Enter scores before or after creating the card
steps.desc: Teachers (or admins) enter assessment scores per subject. Admins: open a subject, then Assessments — the table is Student Name, Class, one column per grading field labelled like CA (/20), and Total. Double-click a cell (or double-tap on mobile) to type a number from 0 to that field's max score; press Enter or click away to save. Empty shows as —, first save creates the student's score record, later saves update it. Teachers: open the subject assignment and use Student Assessments — same columns plus a search box, filtered to their assigned class. Totals are the sum of the fields. Letter grades and class/subject positions are calculated on the report card from the grading scheme, not on this table.

blocks.text: Teachers (or admins) enter assessment scores per subject. Admins: open a subject, then Assessments — the table is Student Name, Class, one column per grading field labelled like CA (/20), and Total. Double-click a cell (or double-tap on mobile) to type a number from 0 to that field's max score; press Enter or click away to save. Empty shows as —, first save creates the student's score record, later saves update it. Teachers: open the subject assignment and use Student Assessments — same columns plus a search box, filtered to their assigned class. Totals are the sum of the fields. Letter grades and class/subject positions are calculated on the report card from the grading scheme, not on this table.

steps.step: Open Student Report for the term
steps.desc: From Academic Sessions, open the term (subsession) and click Student Report. The page title is Student Report, subtitle All students in this subsession with their report card status. You need the student_report permission (create, edit, or read) unless you are Super Admin.

blocks.text: From Academic Sessions, open the term (subsession) and click Student Report. The page title is Student Report, subtitle All students in this subsession with their report card status. You need the student_report permission (create, edit, or read) unless you are Super Admin.
Columns: Student Name, Admission No., Class, Report Status, Actions. Report Status is No Report, Draft (created but not published), or Published.

items.content: Attendance is marked per student, per class, per term, for one calendar date at a time. Statuses are Present, Absent, and Excused. Admins mark from the class Attendance tab or from a student's Attendance calendar; teachers mark from their class Session Attendance page.

steps.desc: Open a class, pick the term, then Attendance. The heading is {term name} — Attendance with the term start and end dates underneath. You need classes.edit (or Super Admin) to change marks. The grid lists every student in the class with a cell per school date in the term.

items.title: Grade Management
items.content: Grades come from three places that must match: the grading template (fields, max scores, letter-grade ranges, traits), the scores entered per subject per student per term, and the report card that totals those scores, assigns a letter grade, and ranks the class.

steps.step: Define fields and grade letters on the template
steps.desc: Under Templates → Grading, the assigned template owns the assessment fields (name, max score; weights must add to 100%) and the grading scheme (grade letter, min range, max range from 0–100% with no overlap). Behavioural traits on the same template appear on the report card. Changing a published template that is already assigned is locked — see Grading Templates in this guide.

blocks.text: Under Templates → Grading, the assigned template owns the assessment fields (name, max score; weights must add to 100%) and the grading scheme (grade letter, min range, max range from 0–100% with no overlap). First save for a student creates the score row; later saves update it. Students with no record show —. Total is the sum of the field scores. There is no separate Submit button.

steps.step: How totals, grades, and positions are calculated
steps.desc: On the student's Report tab, each subject Total is the sum of that subject's field scores. Grand Total sums every subject on the card. The letter Grade is the grading-scheme band that contains (total ÷ max possible) × 100. Subject Position is the rank in the class for that subject this term. Class Avg, Position, and Students on the report header come from the same class set. Positions update as scores are saved — you do not run a separate calculate step.

items.title: Fee Bills & Payments
items.content: Fee Billing Management has three tabs: Bills, School Accounts, and Income & Expenses. Bills are created from a fee bill template, assigned to students or classes, then collected as payments on each recipient. School Accounts (bank + Paystack) has its own topic. This topic covers Bills, recording payments, bill reports, and Income & Expenses.

steps.desc: Go to Fee Billing Management (subtitle Manage school fees, billing, and bank accounts). Tabs: Bills, School Accounts, Income & Expenses. You need bill_income_expense create/edit/delete (or Super Admin) for bills and transactions.

steps.desc: Every fee is created from a fee bill template. The template sets bill items, total amount, currency, and installment options. If none exist, Add New Fee shows No fee bill template yet and a link to Templates → Fee Bill. See Fee Bill Templates in this guide.
